This plot is just a small corner of my shamba — only 0.08 hectares — where I grow cassava and some pigeon peas together. Here in Mtwara the rains come twice a year and the soil is sandy, so I do not buy chemical fertilizer or irrigate this little plot; it would cost too much for such a small piece. I will spread some manure from my goats to keep the soil alive, and my wife and children will work here about twelve days over the season, weeding and harvesting. We always use our own saved seeds because they grow well here, and we do not spray chemicals or hire workers for a plot this size.
